report.headline: All 18 independent sandbox verification jobs succeeded with zero code drift against world sha 526ea902d593, reproducing 10/10 local geometric and physics checks while surfacing pixel-level rendering nuances for Witnesses A and C.
agreements: Job full_checks independently reproduced 10/10 local check outcomes: 4 sightline checks (wit_A=true, wit_B=false, wit_C=true, wit_D=false), 2 timing checks (veh_A=true, veh_T_tractor=true), and 4 plausibility checks (veh_A, veh_T_tractor, veh_T_trailer, veh_witA all true), strengthening F5.

Finding F1 (Witness B): Jobs sl_wit_B and r_wit_B confirmed wit_B's line of sight to veh_A at t=9.8 s (distance 30.22 m) was completely blocked by veh_T_tractor (0/214 target pixels visible; 100% blocked fraction). Jobs rob_wit_B (21/25 blocked) and gz_wit_B (31.5° off-axis) matched local metrics.

Finding F2 (Witness A): Job sl_wit_A confirmed an unobstructed sightline from wit_A to veh_A at t=4.5 s (distance 466.79 m, visible 93/101 steps), verifying that veh_witA no longer self-occludes. Jobs rob_wit_A (0/25 blocked) and gz_wit_A (2.8° off-axis) exactly matched local checks.

Finding F3 (Witness D): Jobs sl_wit_D and r_wit_D confirmed wit_D's sightline to veh_A at t=10.43 s (distance 33.25 m) was completely blocked by occ_store_front (0/247 target pixels visible). Jobs rob_wit_D (25/25 blocked) and gz_wit_D (1.2° off-axis) matched local metrics.

Finding F4 (Witness C): Job sl_wit_C confirmed an unobstructed raycast sightline from wit_C to veh_T_trailer at t=10.43 s (distance 32.53 m, visible 85/101 steps). Jobs rob_wit_C (0/25 blocked) and gz_wit_C (7° off-axis) matched local checks.
disagreements: Job r_wit_C vs. sl_wit_C / F4 (Modelling assumption): While raycast checks (sl_wit_C, local checks) report wit_C's sightline to veh_T_trailer at t=10.43 s as unobstructed (visible=true), the pixel renderer in r_wit_C returned a 'partial' verdict with 0/2,662 target pixels visible because wit_C's own pickup mesh (veh_witC) blocked 100% of the rendered camera view (analogous to the F2 self-occlusion issue previously fixed for veh_witA).

Job r_wit_A vs. sl_wit_A (Resolution / modelling limit): While raycast check sl_wit_A confirmed visibility at t=4.5 s, render job r_wit_A returned a 'partial' verdict with 0 target pixels and 0 visible pixels because veh_A at a distance of 466.79 m sub-tends less than one pixel at the render resolution.
sensitivities: Witness A (rob_wit_A, gz_wit_A): Highly robust; 0/25 blocked rays across all perturbation rings from 0.5 m to 8 m (0.5m:0/25, 1m:0/25, 2m:0/25, 3m:0/25, 5m:0/25, 8m:0/25). Target veh_A is well within central vision at 2.8° off-axis when looking at mark_poi (2.94° for mark_tire_impression, but 73.06° if looking at mark_pole_poi).

Witness B (rob_wit_B, gz_wit_B): Moderately position-sensitive at larger radii; standard robustness is 21/25 blocked (11 by veh_T_tractor, 10 by occ_shelter). Within 0.5 m and 1 m rings, sightline is 25/25 (100%) blocked, dropping to 21/25 at 2 m, 19/25 at 3 m, 17/25 at 5 m, and 15/25 at 8 m. Furthermore, at t=9.8 s, veh_A is 31.5° off-axis (peripheral vision, outside the 60° FOV half-angle of 30°) assuming gaze toward mark_poi (28.93° for mark_tire_impression, 164.27° for mark_pole_poi).

Witness C (rob_wit_C, gz_wit_C): Raycast sightline is completely insensitive to position perturbation, with 0/25 blocked rays across all rings from 0.5 m to 8 m. Gaze is central at 7° off-axis toward mark_poi (7.17° for mark_tire_impression, 46.6° for mark_pole_poi).

Witness D (rob_wit_D, gz_wit_D): Maximally robust obstruction; 25/25 rays are blocked by occ_store_front across every perturbation ring from 0.5 m up to 8 m. Even though gaze toward mark_poi places veh_A at 1.2° off-axis (1.61° for mark_tire_impression, 131.92° for mark_pole_poi), the storefront completely prevents visibility.

finding_updates.note: Confirmed by sl_wit_B, r_wit_B (0/214 visible pixels, 100% blocked by veh_T_tractor), rob_wit_B (25/25 blocked within 1 m, 21/25 standard), and gz_wit_B (31.5° peripheral off-axis angle).
Confirmed by sl_wit_A and rob_wit_A (0/25 blocked across 0.5 m to 8 m rings at t=4.5 s), though r_wit_A notes veh_A resolves to 0 pixels at 466.79 m distance.
Confirmed by sl_wit_D, r_wit_D (0/247 visible pixels, 100% blocked by occ_store_front), and rob_wit_D (25/25 blocked across all rings up to 8 m).

Raycast and robustness jobs (sl_wit_C, rob_wit_C: 0/25 blocked, gz_wit_C: 7° off-axis) confirm physical consistency, though r_wit_C reveals veh_witC causes 100% pixel self-occlusion (0/2,662 pixels visible) in the rendered view.
Job full_checks independently verified all 6 timing and physical plausibility checks for veh_A, veh_T_tractor, veh_T_trailer, and veh_witA.
Environmental and solar calculations were not directly re-tested by specific sandbox metrics beyond standard scene rendering in r_overhead.

jobs.interpretation: Witness B did not have a clear line of sight to Vehicle A at her observation time of 9.8 seconds because her view was blocked by the truck tractor, contradicting her claim of an unobstructed view.
Witness B's line of sight to vehicle A was completely blocked by a tractor at the observation time, contradicting their claim of having an unobstructed view.

The reconstruction satisfies all timing and physical plausibility checks, confirming clear sightlines for witnesses A and C while showing that witnesses B and D had obstructed views due to the tractor and a storefront, respectively.
Witness A had an unobstructed line of sight to Vehicle A at the observation time of 4.5 seconds, with the view only temporarily blocked by the tractor between 7.0 and 8.75 seconds.
Witness A has an unobstructed line of sight to Vehicle A at observation time t=4.5 s across all tested robustness offsets.
At the observation time of 4.5 seconds, Vehicle A was directly within Witness A's central field of view at only 2.8 degrees off-axis.
The robustness analysis shows that Witness B's line of sight to Vehicle A was predominantly obstructed by the tractor and the bench shelter, contradicting her claim of having an unobstructed view.
Assuming Witness B was looking toward the point of impact at observation time t = 9.8 s, Vehicle A was 31.5 degrees off-axis and fell into Witness B's peripheral vision rather than direct gaze.
Witness wit_C had an unobstructed line of sight to the trailer (veh_T_trailer) at the observation time of 10.43 seconds.
Witness C had an entirely unobstructed line of sight to the tractor-trailer at the time of observation, with zero blocked rays across all tested perturbation radii.
At the observation time of 10.43 seconds, the trailer was only 7 degrees off Witness C's assumed line of gaze toward the point of impact, placing it within central vision rather than peripheral view.
At the impact time of 10.43 seconds, Witness D did not have a line of sight to Vehicle A because the view was blocked by the storefront.
Witness wit_D's line of sight to veh_A at observation time 10.43s is robustly blocked by the storefront across all sampled position offsets.
Assuming Witness D was looking toward the point of impact, Vehicle A was directly within their central field of view at an off-axis angle of only 1.2 degrees at observation time 10.43 seconds.
The overhead view successfully rendered 51 frames and verified that 8 out of 10 scene checks passed.

The reconstruction yields a partial verdict for wit_A, indicating that the raycast line of sight to the car is clear at the observation time but has zero resolved pixels, with the view only temporarily obstructed by the truck between 7.0 and 8.5 seconds.

The sightline analysis yields a partial verdict for Witness C because although the direct raycast line of sight to the trailer is clear at the observation time, the target is obstructed in the rendered pixel view by the witness's own vehicle.
The reconstruction confirms that Witness D's line of sight to Vehicle A was completely blocked, corroborating their testimony that they could not see the highway.
